# Week 1 Training Analysis

## 1. Weekly Summary

**What was trained:**
- 4 of 5 planned sessions completed (Lower Shape skipped entirely)
- Lower Power, Upper Strength, Run + Core, Upper Hypertrophy, partial Speed Conditioning
- Total high-intensity work: 2 lower body days, 2 upper body days, 1 conditioning session

**Volume highlights:**
- **Strong lifts:** Trap bar DL 140kg x 2x8 (RPE 9), Barbell row 80kg (RPE 8)
- **Decent upper work:** DB bench 68kg, Weighted pull-ups +10kg x 3 sets
- **Conditioning:** Pushed hard on intervals (10 rounds instead of 8, RPE 9)
- **Incomplete sessions:** Upper Hypertrophy severely truncated (only 1-2 sets per exercise), core work skipped, speed work mostly skipped

**Red flags:**
- Multiple incomplete workouts suggest fatigue or time constraints
- Upper Hypertrophy session particularly affected (noted 750m farmer carries earlier same day)
- Split squat instability issue noted

## 2. Progressive Overload Recommendations

### Lower Power (Week 2):
- **Trap bar DL:** Drop to **135kg for 3x8** (RPE 9 for 2 sets is too aggressive this early; add a set, reduce weight slightly)
- **Split squat:** Stay at **22kg but use flat surface**, focus on stability, 3x8 per leg
- **Box/Squat jump:** Increase to **3x6 reps** at same height
- **Nordic curls:** Continue bodyweight, aim for **3x4-5 controlled reps**
- **Calf raise:** Increase to **85kg single-leg** on leg press, 3x12

### Upper Strength (Week 2):
- **Bench press (DB):** Increase to **70kg (35kg DBs), 3x6-8** (RPE 8 is perfect training zone)
- **Weighted pull-up:** Increase to **12.5kg, 3x5-6 reps** (RPE 6 means plenty in reserve)
- **Barbell row:** Increase to **82.5kg, 3x8** (solid RPE 8)
- **Face pull/Rear delt:** Maintain **32kg, add 1 set** (3x12-15)

### Run + Core (Week 2):
- **Intervals:** Return to prescribed **8 rounds of 30s/90s rest** (you did 10x30s/60s at RPE 9—too much)
- **Farmer carry:** Increase to **32kg per hand, 3x30-40m**
- **COMPLETE THE CORE WORK:** Side plank 3x30s each side, Dead bug 3x10

### Upper Hypertrophy (Week 2):
- **DO NOT schedule heavy carries same day**
- **Incline DB press:** **70kg for 3x10-12** (you only did 1 set at 80kg/RPE 9)
- **Lat pulldown:** **77.5kg for 3x8-10** (reduce slightly to complete full volume)
- **Lateral raise:** **12kg for 3x12-15** (complete all sets)
- **EZ curl:** **22.5kg for 3x10-12**
- **OH tricep ext:** **32kg DB for 3x10-12**
- **Rear delt row:** **25kg for 3x12** (30kg at RPE 10 for only 5 reps is too heavy)

### Speed Conditioning (Week 2):
- **COMPLETE THIS SESSION**
- **Ankle mobility:** 2x10 circles each direction + 2x30s calf stretch
- **Tib raises:** 3x15-20 bodyweight
- **Add:** 2-3 sets of low pogo jumps or ankle bounces (low intensity ankle plyos)

## 3. Ankle Recovery Notes

**Ankle feel: 4/5** — This is solid, but there are concerns

# WEEK 2 TRAINING ANALYSIS

## 1. WEEKLY SUMMARY

**What Was Trained:**
- 4 training sessions: Lower Power, Upper Strength, Lower Shape, Speed/Power

- Plyometric work (pogos, verticals, depth drops)
- Main strength lifts (trap bar DL, bench, rows, pull-ups)

**Overall:** Solid week with good strength progressions. Data tracking needs tightening.

w6.text:
# Training Log Analysis — Week 6

---

## Weekly Summary

**Sessions completed:** 5 (Lower Power, Upper Strength, Zone 2/Core, Upper Hypertrophy, Speed/Power)

**Training split:** Well-rounded week hitting all major qualities — aerobic base, maximal strength, hypertrophy, power, and sprint work. Good frequency distribution.

**Volume highlights:**
- Deadlift: 140kg across 4+3+2+2 = **11 total reps** at near-maximal loading
- Upper volume was substantial across two separate sessions — significant shoulder and pulling stimulus
- Handstand press programming (85/90/93/95%) indicates serious overhead strength development
- Sprint + plyometric session completes the speed-strength continuum well

**Overall:** High quality week. Volume is appropriate for a 106kg athlete with a conservative injury history. No obvious junk volume. The coached group context means intensity was externally regulated — a plus.

---

## Progressive Overload

**Deadlift (140kg, 4/3/2/2):**
> Next week: **142.5kg, target 4/3/3/2**
> Rationale: Sets 3 and 4 dropped to 2 reps — not yet owning 140kg. Add 2.5kg and chase one extra rep on set 3 before jumping further.

**Handstand Press (wave load at 85/90/93/95%):**
> Next week: **Keep percentages identical, target 5/4/3/2+**
> Rationale: The 2+ on the top set suggests near-failure. Consolidate this wave by adding one rep to sets 1 and 2 before loading progresses. If percentages are off a 1RM estimate, retest or add 2.5kg to your working reference weight only if set 1 felt genuinely controlled.

**Dips (10 reps, E4MOM x4):**
> Next week: **Add 5kg, target 3x8 + 1x6+ (belt/vest)**
> If bodyweight felt easy across all 4 rounds, load is overdue. If it was a grind, stay bodyweight and target **4x10 with 2 RIR minimum.**

**Lateral Raise + Shoulder Press complex:**
> Next week: **Increase lateral raise weight by 2kg** (keep the complex structure identical)
> The bottleneck here is the lateral raise — that dictates press weight. Small jump preserves the conditioning stimulus.

**Chin-ups (Tabata + park session):**
> No load data provided. Next week: **Log reps per set.** If bodyweight feels manageable for 8+ reps consistently, add **5kg for the strength session chin-ups specifically.**

**5km run (5:06/km, RPE 7):**
> Next week: **Target 5:00/km at same RPE 7**
> 6 seconds/km improvement is realistic. If ankle feel drops below 7/10, hold pace and prioritize feel over split.

---

## Ankle Recovery

**Problem:** No ankle feel scores were logged this week.

**This is a gap — fix it immediately.**

For a 106kg athlete with right ankle history, subjective feel scores are your earliest warning system. Before next week's sessions:

- **Log ankle feel 0–10 before and after every session**
- Pay specific attention to: **Lower Power session** (running impact) and **Speed/Power session** (sprint + plyometric loading — highest ankle stress of the week)
- The calf raises in the park session are useful rehab stimulus *if* they were single-leg. Confirm and log which variation

**Provisional guidance based on session selection:**
- Sprints + plyometrics in the same week as a 5km run is aggressive for a conservatively managed ankle. If scores come in below **6/10** on any session day, **drop the plyometric volume by 50%** the following week and flag to your coach.
- No changes recommended *yet* — but flying blind without scores means you're managing this reactively, not proactively.

---

## Focus Points

**1. Log the damn ankle scores**
Every session, pre and post. One number. This is non-negotiable given your history and current training load. Without it, progressive overload decisions on lower body work are guesswork.

**2. Own 140kg before adding load**
Your deadlift rep distribution (4/3/2/2) shows fatigue drop-off across the session. Priority next week is **better set 3 and 4 execution at 142.5kg**, not chasing 145kg. Positional quality at 106kg bodyweight under fatigue is where injuries happen.

**3. Protect shoulder recovery between the two upper sessions**
You hit substantial shoulder volume in both Upper Strength *and* Upper Hypertrophy — that's a significant weekly stimulus. Ensure **48–72 hours between upper sessions** is maintained next week. If soreness is still present going into the second upper session, reduce handstand press volume by one set, not intensity.

# Week 8 Training Analysis

---

## Weekly Summary

**Sessions completed:** 4 (2 full training sessions, 1 mobility/recovery, 1 easy KB session)

**What was trained:**
- Lower body strength: Low bar squat (105kg 3×5)
- Upper push: Bench press (80kg 3×10), DB shoulder press (16kg 3×10)
- Upper pull: Chin-ups (3×fail), pull-ups (3×10 mixed grip)
- Posterior chain: RDL (60kg 1×10)
- Conditioning: 20min Zone 2 rowing
- Accessory/stability: Band work, dead bugs, leg raises, balance pad drills
- Mobility: Dedicated 25min session (illness-driven)

**Overall volume:** Below normal. Two sessions were significantly compromised — one by a headache/low nutrition, one by illness (swollen throat, body aches). Effective hard training was essentially limited to **two sessions** this week.

**Highlights:**
- Squat at 105kg × 3×5 @ RPE 7 is a solid data point — good load management
- Pulling volume was reasonable across the week despite circumstances
- Smart decision to swap the hypertrophy session for mobility while sick

---

## Progressive Overload

**Low Bar Squat**
- Current: 105kg × 3×5 @ RPE 7
- **Next week: 110kg × 3×5, target RPE 7–7.5**
- RPE 7 with 105kg suggests room to move. Standard 5kg jump is appropriate at this load for a 106kg athlete. If RPE hits 8+ on set 1, drop back to 107.5kg if plates allow.

**Bench Press**
- Current: 80kg × 3×10 @ RPE 7 (after a 60kg warm-up set — treat the 60kg as prep, not a working set)
- **Next week: 82.5kg × 3×10, target RPE 7–7.5**
- 80kg for 3×10 @ RPE 7 is comfortably within capacity. Small 2.5kg jump keeps progress honest without spiking fatigue after a compromised week.

**Pull-Ups (mixed grip)**
- Current: 3×10 @ RPE 7
- **Next week: 4×10 same RPE, or 3×10 with a 2–3 second eccentric on each rep**
- Adding a set is the simplest progression here. The eccentric tempo option builds more pulling strength with the same weight — useful given chin-up reps dropped (8/6/5) suggesting fatigue accumulation.

**Chin-Ups**
- Current: 3×fail → 8/6/5 reps
- **Next week: Target 3×8 — stop 1 rep short of failure each set**
- The drop-off from 8 to 5 suggests going to failure too early. Capping at 8 conserves quality and will likely net the same or more total volume (24 reps vs 19 this week).

**DB Shoulder Press**
- Current: 16kg × 3×10 @ RPE 6
- **Next week: 18kg × 3×10, target RPE 7**
- RPE 6 is leaving too much on the table. Move to the next dumbbell up.

**RDL**
- Current: 60kg × 1×10 @ RPE 5 — this is essentially a warm-up set, not a training stimulus
- **Next week: 3×10 @ 80–85kg, target RPE 7**
- Single set at RPE 5 provides no meaningful posterior chain stimulus for a 106kg athlete. This needs volume and load. If 80kg feels easy at rep 5, it's right. If form breaks, stay at 80kg and build sets first.

---

## Ankle Recovery

**Score: 4/5 — stable and positive**

This is the best indicator you can have at week 8 with an ankle history. Key observations:

- Balance pad drills were included and completed — continue these as a non-negotiable weekly staple, not an optional add-on
- Calf tightness noted after the KB session — this is worth monitoring. A tight calf at 106kg can load the ankle joint indirectly, particularly under squatting and hinging patterns
- **Action:** Add 2×45 second calf stretches (straight knee + bent knee, both positions) post every session. This directly addresses the tightness noted and reduces downstream ankle stress
- **No need to reduce loading** based on the 4/5 score. Maintain current ankle work volume
- If score drops to 3/5 or below, flag before squatting heavy — do not push through ankle discomfort under a loaded bar

---

## Focus Points

**1. Rebuild training quality after illness — don't compensate with volume**
Two of four sessions were compromised. The instinct after a down week is to do extra.

## Weekly Summary

**What was trained:** Full body across two coached sessions — KB conditioning (hinge, squat, push, pull) plus speed/power work (plyometrics, bodyweight conditioning, cardio capacity).

**Overall volume:** Moderate-high. KB session was the primary strength stimulus (28kg, 20-min EMOM = roughly 75 swings, 50 goblet squats, 40 push presses, 60 rows + max push-ups). Speed session was predominantly cardiovascular/neuromuscular with meaningful plyo load (jumping lunges, burpees, jump rope).

**Highlights:**
- Ankle feel at 5/5 — best possible score, a genuine green light
- KB smoker was the quality strength session of the week; 20 min EMOM at 28kg for 106kg athlete is solid baseline work
- Two HR sessions logged (avg 125/136) shows good aerobic engagement without redlining
- Jump rope and jumping lunges completed without issue — meaningful for ankle confidence

---

## Progressive Overload

**KB Swings (28kg):**
Next week target — move to **32kg** for the EMOM sets. If 32kg isn't available, stay at 28kg but increase finisher target: aim **25+ unbroken** swings versus whatever was hit this week.

**Goblet Squats (28kg):**
Move to **32kg** next week. Depth and tempo cue — 3 seconds down, pause 1 second at the bottom. Don't just add load without owning the range.

**KB Push Press (28kg):**
Stay at **28kg**, increase reps from 8 to **10 per set**. Push press is more technical and shoulder-dependent — rep increase before load increase here.

**KB Rows (28kg):**
Move to **32kg**, keep at 12 reps. Row can handle load faster than the press.

**Push-ups (max effort):**
Log the actual number achieved in the max sets next week. Without a baseline number recorded this week, track it properly so there's something to beat in Week 11.

**Bodyweight plyos (jumping lunges, burpees):**
No load to progress, but target **HR above 140 average** for the speed session next week — push the intensity ceiling slightly now that ankle is confirmed 5/5.

---

## Ankle Recovery

**Score: 5/5 — no restrictions warranted.**

This is the first clear signal to cautiously increase impact load. Jumping lunges and jump rope were completed this week — that's meaningful. Do not back off now, but also don't spike volume recklessly.

**One specific change:** Jump rope can move from station work to a standalone warm-up tool. Add **2 minutes of continuous jump rope** at the start of the speed session next week as an ankle loading/proprioception check before the main session begins. If it feels off at any point, that's your early warning system.

**No other modifications needed.** Conservative approach has paid off — 9 weeks of managed loading has earned this score.

---

## Focus Points

**1. Test the 32kg KB this week.**
Ankle confidence is high, body is adapted to 28kg across multiple movement patterns. The KB jump is the single highest-leverage strength progression available right now. Don't drift another week at the same load.

**2. Log your push-up numbers.**
Max push-up sets are built into the programming but there's no recorded baseline. Write down the number every time. Without data, there's nothing to beat and no progression to manage.

**3. Keep HR honest in the speed sessions.**
Avg 125–136 is moderate. At 106kg with a 5/5 ankle, you can afford to push closer to **145–150 avg** in the speed/conditioning sessions. That's where actual cardiovascular adaptation happens. Don't coast through the plyo stations — treat them as genuine work intervals.
